title: First-wave ClawHub malware skills by jordanprater, danman60, gpaitai and lvy19811120-gif (openclawcli.zip / ClawdAuthenticatorTool.zip lures)
summary: Alongside the Aslaep123 and zaycv clusters, OpenSourceMalware's audit of ClawHub identified further named skills from four other accounts published between 2026-01-27 and 2026-02-02 that use the same social-engineering pattern: legitimate-looking documentation for YouTube, X/Twitter, Yahoo Finance, proxy-scraping and Polymarket utilities, plus a mandatory "authentication tool" the victim must download (`openclawcli.zip`, `ClawdAuthenticatorTool.zip`) or a base64-into-bash command. All of them route to the same command-and-control infrastructure at 91.92.242.30 and steal exchange API keys, wallet private keys, SSH credentials and browser passwords.
details:
**Per-skill technique, as tabulated by OpenSourceMalware:**

| Author | Skill | Payload delivery |
|---|---|---|
| jordanprater | `twittertrends`, `xtrends`, `yahoofinance`, `youtube-summarize`, `youtube-video-downloader`, `youtube-thumbnail-grabber` | download `openclawcli.zip` |
| danman60 | `proxy-scrap` | download `ClawdAuthenticatorTool.zip` |
| gpaitai | `polymarket` | download `PolymarketAuthTool.zip` |
| lvy19811120-gif | `polymarket-prediction-agent` | `bash` + base64 |

The same audit explicitly records two skills from these accounts as **not** malicious (`danman60/tesla-skill`, `jordanprater/polymarketcli`, plus `zaycv/novafon`); they are listed here only so that readers do not over-block by author.

**Volume context:** the audit counted 386 malicious skills in total, dominated by `hightower6eu` (354) which republished each template dozens of times; those bulk clones are tracked in SKA-2026-0001 (ClawHavoc). This advisory records the distinctly named first-wave skills so that lockfiles and blocklists can match them exactly.

**Fact vs. inference:** author names, skill names, payload technique and the shared C2 IP are as published by OpenSourceMalware (2026-02-01, updated 2026-02-02 and 2026-02-03). Attribution of all accounts to one operator is not asserted — the sources report shared infrastructure and shared tradecraft only.

**2026-08-04 update — second-stage behaviour of the X/Twitter trends skill.** SlowMist's MistEye team analysed the high-download `X (Twitter) Trends` skill from this wave and published the full chain: the base64 block in SKILL.md decodes to a download-and-execute of `q0c7ew2ro8l2cfqp` from 91.92.242.30, which fetches the second stage `dyrtvwjfveyxjf23`. Dynamically, the second stage fakes a macOS system password dialog, validates the captured password, then archives host information plus `.txt`/`.pdf` files from Desktop, Documents and Downloads and uploads the ZIP to `hxxps://socifiapp[.]com/api/reports/upload`. SlowMist reports `socifiapp[.]com` as registered 2025-07-14 and already flagged as malicious remote-control infrastructure, and notes reported overlap between 91.92.242.30 and Poseidon-stealer infrastructure — attribution we relay but have not verified. This confirms that the first-stage payload is only an entry point: blocking the skill names below does not cover the second-stage C2. Verified 2026-08-04.
